clue.text: "Crossing a Line" by a dramatist

parts.note: Ben Travers was the English writer of the Aldwych farces

explanation.surface: A play called Crossing a Line, credited to some playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it look like a play title; in the answer the dramatist comes first, with 'by' only joining him to A and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A traversal is the act of going across something, so it is a crossing.

clue.text: Sound conductor

definitions.meaning: to make a series of short sharp knocking noises
Sir Simon ..., the British orchestral conductor

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a clattering noise and the surname of the famous conductor Sir Simon.

clue.text: Come to church in Italy

CE is the Church of England abbreviation

explanation.surface: An invitation to come along to a church service in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordius uses 'in Italy' as a definition by location: the answer is a city in Italy. 'to' just joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is a place found in Italy, so the setter defines it by its location.

clue.text: Summary turnover of one of nine held by soldier

indicators.note: held by means the soldier's letters enclose the other piece

explanation.surface: A summary of staff turnover in a team of nine, held by a soldier.

explanation.definitionFit: A résumé is a short summary of something longer, as in a précis.

clue.text: A right in a wrong is still a wrong

indicators.note: in places the first letter and the abbreviation for right inside the wrong

parts.note: a vice is a moral failing or wrong

explanation.surface: A moralising maxim: putting a right inside a wrong still leaves a wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: AR goes inside A VICE, after its first two letters; 'is still' just links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Greed is one of the seven deadly sins, so it is a moral wrong.

clue.text: Sweet girl holding tummy that's gone pear-shaped?

explanation.surface: A girl with a tummy that has turned pear-shaped, perhaps from too many sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's gone pear-shaped' moves the first letter of the tummy word to its end, giving LLYBE; 'holding' sets that between JE and AN.
explanation.definitionFit: A jelly bean is a small chewy confection, so a type of sweet.

clue.text: Brown carries paper confusing one act of policy made on the hoof

definitions.text: of policy made on the hoof

indicators.note: carries means the prime minister holds the paper inside

parts.note: Gordon Brown was Prime Minister, PM, when this puzzle appeared
rag is slang for a poor newspaper

indicators.note: confusing tells us to mix up the letters of one act

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister carries a newspaper that muddles a policy decision made in haste.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown here is Gordon Brown, the UK Prime Minister, not a colour. 'confusing' turns I + ACT into ATIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A pragmatic policy is practical, decided by circumstance rather than principle, as though improvised.

clue.text: Proust's memorable cake

parts.note: In Proust's novel, tasting a small sponge cake dipped in tea brings back a flood of childhood memories

explanation.definitionFit: The small shell-shaped sponge cake famously triggers involuntary memory in Proust's In Search of Lost Time.

clue.text: Plant makes a sound shopping bag for Sheila

explanation.walkthrough: In a caricatured Australian accent 'carrier' comes out close to the plant's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerria is a yellow-flowered shrub of the rose family, so a garden plant.

clue.text: Dodgy win, as last King of Poland

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A suspicious election win for Poland's final monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' looks like part of the definition, but it is fodder; the clue is still true, as Stanislaw August Poniatowski was Poland's last king.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanislaw August Poniatowski reigned as the final monarch of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth.

clue.text: Apostle loses heart with one complaint or another

indicators.note: loses heart means the central letters of the name are removed

an ague is a fever, one kind of illness or complaint

explanation.walkthrough: 'loses heart' strips the middle AU, leaving PL. 'another' is the definition: the clue's ague is one complaint, the answer another.
explanation.definitionFit: A plague is an epidemic disease, so another illness or complaint besides the ague.

clue.text: Crime likely to arise during postal strike?

definitions.text: likely to arise during postal strike?
definitions.meaning: striking workers 'black' goods, so blacked letters pile up during a postal strike

explanation.definitionFit: Extortion by threat is a crime, and read whimsically the word is mail that strikers have blacked.

clue.text: A rough beard can scratch

indicators.note: rough means roughed up, so the letters of beard are disordered

explanation.surface: A rough beard can scratch your face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' turns BEARD into BRADE; 'can' joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrade is to scrape or wear away a surface, so to scratch it.

clue.text: One that quivers like a writer on paper

parts.note: as means like
a pen is a writing instrument
a leaf is a sheet of paper

explanation.surface: Someone trembling like a nervous writer before a blank page.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspen's leaves tremble in the slightest breeze; the phrase 'shake like an aspen leaf' is proverbial.

clue.text: Gay psalmist in Maryland

parts.note: camp in its sense of flamboyant, theatrically gay
King David is traditionally the author of the Psalms

explanation.surface: A flamboyant singer of psalms living in Maryland.
explanation.walkthrough: As with 'in Italy' elsewhere, the definition gives the place's location.
explanation.definitionFit: The US presidential retreat lies in the Catoctin Mountains of Maryland, so it is a place there.

clue.text: Accommodation unlet — perhaps it's windy

parts.note: a flat is accommodation

indicators.note: perhaps suggests an alternative arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: An unlet flat might be draughty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns UNLET into ULENT; 'it's' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Flatulent means suffering from gas in the gut, so windy in the digestive sense.

clue.text: Number held in illegal detention

explanation.surface: A number of people held in unlawful custody.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten is a cardinal number.

clue.text: Company where anything goes up

explanation.surface: A permissive firm where anything goes.
explanation.walkthrough: From the saying 'two's company'. OWT is Yorkshire dialect for anything.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'two's company, three's a crowd' makes the number a company.

clue.text: Born not altogether of necessity …

parts.note: need is a necessity

clue.text: Everything in performance lacking in depth

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: a show is a performance
all is everything

explanation.surface: A performance that throws in everything but lacks depth.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shallow lacks depth, literally or figuratively.

clue.text: Dash about to keep 21 in high spirits

clue.text: Unity for which Europe initially gets no backing

clue.text: … during which rises an aroma

explanation.definitionFit: Nascent describes the early stage during which something is arising or being born.

clue.text: They go abroad to get a girl into kinky sex

clue.text: Many dress with ill intent

clue.text: One boils as we rest from working

clue.text: Writer was better beheaded?

clue.text: It's sweet to take me to a Greek city
